messages.content: ok need a sanity check on falcon terms before i send the LOI draft to the team tmrw. target is Nimbus Logistics (NMBL). LTM EBITDA 142m, net debt ~310m, 27.0m shares fully diluted. stock closed 31.05 today. corvane IC approved a range of 9.0x to 9.75x. i'm thinking we lead at 9.5x. whats the implied price per share + premium

Here's the math at 9.5x LTM EBITDA:

- Enterprise value: 9.5 × $142M = $1,349M
- Less net debt: $1,349M − $310M = $1,039M equity value
- Per share: $1,039M ÷ 27.0M = ~$38.48
- Premium to the $31.05 close: ~23.9%

At the ends of the IC range:
- 9.0x → EV $1,278M, equity $968M, ~$35.85/share (~15.5% premium)
- 9.75x → EV $1,384.5M, equity $1,074.5M, ~$39.80/share (~28.2% premium)

A premium in the mid-20s is within the usual range for a strategic buyer, though it depends on recent trading and how their board views standalone value.
ok round to 38.50/sh. thats the number. also the board (theirs) meets 2026-10-29, I want the LOI in their hands before that so call it LOI out by 2026-10-28. exclusivity ask 45 days

Got it. $38.50 per share is a ~24.0% premium to $31.05 and implies about $1,349.5M EV at the same net debt (~9.50x). On timing: an LOI delivered by 2026-10-28 gives their board one day before the 2026-10-29 meeting, which is tight; you might give their banker a heads-up earlier. A 45-day exclusivity ask is common at this size, but expect pushback toward 30 days.
they'll push back for sure. what about break fee, i was going to propose 3% of equity value. also flag for me what diligence items matter most for a 3PL like nimbus

3% of ~$1,039.5M equity value is about $31.2M, inside the usual 2–4% band. For a third-party logistics company, the diligence items that usually matter most:

1. Customer concentration and contract terms (renewal dates, termination rights)
2. Quality of earnings: how much EBITDA is one-off fuel surcharge or pass-through revenue
3. Labor: union agreements, driver turnover, any open organizing efforts
4. Real estate and lease obligations at the main hubs
5. Technology: WMS/TMS systems and any planned replatforming
6. Insurance and claims history

good. customer concentration is the big one, their top customer is ~22% of revenue and that contract renews 2027-03-31. memphis hub has a union contract up next year too. We agreed internally that QoE goes to Ashby & Rowe (outside accountants), kickoff after LOI. pls draft me 3 bullet summary of terms for the team email

Here's a three-bullet summary for the team:

- **Price:** $38.50 per share in cash for Nimbus Logistics (NMBL), a ~24% premium to the $31.05 close, implying ~9.5x LTM EBITDA of $142M
- **Process:** LOI out by 2026-10-28, ahead of the Nimbus board meeting on 2026-10-29; 45 days of exclusivity requested; proposed break fee of 3% of equity value (~$31.2M)
- **Diligence focus:** top-customer concentration (~22% of revenue, contract renews 2027-03-31), the Memphis hub union contract, and a quality-of-earnings review by Ashby & Rowe starting after the LOI
